title: Beets, fresh, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Beets are a root vegetable belonging to the Amaranthaceae family. Fresh beets have a deep red, sometimes purple hue, a mildly sweet flavor, and a firm, juicy texture. When cooked without added fat they retain most of their vitamins, minerals, and natural color.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beets contain betanin, a natural pigment that gives them their characteristic color and antioxidant properties.
Ancient cultures used beets both as food and for medicinal purposes.
Beets come in red and golden varieties, both nutritionally rich.
Beet juice is often used as a natural food coloring and in cosmetics.
In many countries beet soup (borscht) is traditional, but beets are also enjoyed boiled, roasted, or in salads.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Betanin and other polyphenols help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Nitrate compounds promote vasodilation, improving circulation and lowering blood pressure.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Provides vitamins and minerals
items.content: Beets supply vitamin C, folate, potassium, magnesium, and iron, essential for metabolism and blood formation.

items.title: Aids liver detoxification
items.content: Glucosinolates in beets help the body eliminate toxins.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Beets contain oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Blood sugar impact
items.content: Natural sugars can affect blood glucose levels, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergy to beets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beets can be eaten raw in salads, boiled as a side dish, roasted, steamed, or juiced. When cooking without added fat, steam or simmer in a small amount of water to preserve nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh beets in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, loosely packed in a perforated bag, for up to 2–3 weeks. Cooked beets should be kept in an airtight container in the fridge and consumed within 5 days.
